summary: Rajendra Chandra Hazra was an Indology scholar who earned his B.A. at the University of Dhaka (~1926–1929) and completed his doctorate under Sushil Kumar De (~1931–1936). He held posts at Jagannath University (1931), Dhaka (1939–1951), and Sanskrit College (1951–1972).

Rajendralal Mitra worked in Indology, history, and archaeology after studying at Hindu School, Medical College, Kolkata (1837–1841), and the University of Calcutta. He served at The Asiatic Society (librarian-cum-assistant-secretary 1846–1856; president 1885) and directed Wards' Institution (1856–1881).

Rajesh P. N. Rao works in computational fields and Indology. He studied at Angelo State University (~1989–1993) and under Dana H. Ballard at the University of Rochester (~1993–1998), becoming a Professor of Computer Science at the University of Washington in 2000.

Rajkrishna Mukhopadhyay was a history and archaeology scholar who studied at Krishnagar Government College and Presidency University (~1864–1868). He later held posts at Presidency University and Scottish Church College.

Raju Rimal works in Indology, history, and archaeology. His posts include serving on the editorial board of Documenta Nepalica (attested 2018) and working at the National Archives of Nepal (attested 2018).

Rakhal Das Banerji studied history at Presidency University (~1903–1907) and the University of Calcutta (~1907–1911). A scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology, he served in the Archaeological Survey of India (1911–1926) and held a professorship at Banaras Hindu University (1928–1930).
Rakra Tethong Rinpoche studied under Trijang Rinpoche and Gendun Chopel (~1946–1950).

Ralf Kramer is a Tibetologist who earned an MA at the University of Hamburg (-1997), studied at the University of London, and was taught by David P. Jackson. He held librarian positions at the Indian Institute, Oxford, and the Bodleian Library.

Ralph Abraham studied at the University of Michigan (1952–1960) and with Debabrata Sensharma. Active in philosophy and other fields, he held appointments at UC Berkeley (1960–1962), Columbia (1962–1964), Princeton (1964–1968), and UC Santa Cruz (associate professor 1968, professor 1980).
Ralph Lerner is a philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Chicago under Leo Strauss (~1947–1953). He later held a post at the University of Chicago (~1953).

Ralph Lilley Turner was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Christ's College, Cambridge (~1906–1910). He held posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1913), Banaras Hindu University (1920–1922), and SOAS and the University of London (1922–1957).

Ralph T. H. Griffith studied at The Queen's College, Oxford (~1843–1846) under Horace Hayman Wilson. An Indologist, he served as Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford (1849), Principal at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1861–1878), and in the Indian Education Service (~1853–1885).

Ralph Waldo Emerson was a scholar of philosophy and other fields. He completed his studies at Harvard University and Harvard College (~1817–1821) and later attended Harvard Divinity School (~1825–1826).
Ram Chandra Dhungana worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He held assistant editor posts at Ancient Nepal (attested 1973) and the Archaeological Survey of India (attested 1974).

Ram Chandra Kak studied at Sri Pratap College (~1909–1913) and under John Marshall (1914–1919). Active in history, archaeology, and Indology, he held posts at Sri Pratap Singh Museum (1913–1919) and Jammu and Kashmir's archaeology department (~1919–1930).

Ram Chandra Pandeya was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology who studied under Vasudev Vishwanath Gokhale and T. R. V. Murti. He held appointments at the University of Delhi, including head of Buddhist Studies (~1966–1973) and acharya (~1973–1996).

Ram Karan Sharma was an Indologist and linguist educated at Patna University and UC Berkeley under Murray Barnson Emeneau (PhD ~1957–1959). He served as vice chancellor of Kameshwar Singh Darbhanga Sanskrit University (1974–1980) and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1984–1985).

Ram Mohan Roy was active in religious studies, philosophy, and Indology. He founded several organizations and institutions, including the Atmiya Sabha (1814), Presidency University (1816), Anglo-Hindu School (1822), Vedanta College (1826), and Brahmo Samaj (1828).

Ram Niwas Pandey was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who completed his doctoral studies under Hit Narayan Jha. He studied at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University and the Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya Institute of Archaeology.

Ram Shankar Bhattacharya studied Indology and philosophy under Raghunatha Shastri. He held research assistant posts at Banaras Hindu University and the All-India Kashiraj Trust, as well as a teaching post at Tikmani Sanskrit Mahavidyalaya.
